labels: silver — measures agreement with cited tasks, not correctness

coverage.note: a pair is servable when the chapter of its labelled task holds at least one task row; unservable pairs are unanswerable by construction, not by retrieval failure

ceiling.note: a pair is answerable when the labelled task is in the corpus; the headline pool cannot exceed this fraction no matter how good retrieval is

pools.label: ALL pairs — THE HEADLINE. Quote this number.

ANSWERABLE pairs — the labelled task is in the corpus, so retrieval could have found it. THE ENGINE'S SCORE. Every other pair is a missing manual, not a missed retrieval. Never quote this as overall performance.
UNANSWERABLE pairs — the labelled task is not in the corpus at all. Strict recall here is 0 by construction; relaxed can be non-zero when a sibling task is held.
SERVABLE chapters only — NOT the headline. Excludes every pair whose chapter has no corpus, so it answers 'how well does retrieval work where a corpus exists', nothing broader.
UNSERVABLE chapters only — expected ~0 by construction (nothing indexed to retrieve). Anything above 0 is a finding.
